The School Governors
The governing body at Oaklands Schools works with the Co-Headteacher and the staff to decide the schools’ aims and policies and to oversee the efficient running of the school.
We have particular responsibility for:
The Local Governing Body is a Committee of the Corvus Learning Trust.
Agreeing targets to raise standards of achievement.
Dealing with complaints about the schools.
Ever considered becoming a School Governor?
The governing body of Oaklands Schools is always interested in recruiting new members who have the skills that we require. We seek individuals who have an awareness of standards in public life, a determination to abide by them and the integrity to participate in collective decision-making in the best interests of the Schools.
Governors will be able to demonstrate:
A commitment to promoting equality and diversity.
Desired skills and experience:
We also have a professional Clerk.
All of our Governors have their own careers and responsibilities but they dedicate time to the schools when they are able. Our Governors bring a wealth of different experience to the Governing Body which is highly valued. We are all volunteers who wish to make a positive contribution to the schools and the education of all its children.
The governing body’s overriding responsibility is to work in partnership with the Executive Headteacher, to promote continuous improvement in the performance of the schools. We play an important part in raising school’s standards through the key roles of setting strategic direction, ensuring accountability and monitoring and evaluating schools performance.
The governing body currently meets twice a term with committees meeting on a regular basis. In addition to the work outlined above, the governors review issues relating to behaviour, curriculum, staffing, building maintenance and finances. The governing body makes collective decisions.
Co-opted governors are appointed for a term of 4 years by the governing body to ensure the body has a range of skills and expertise amongst members. We encourage all our governors to attend the excellent training provided by the local authority to ensure we maintain the skills necessary to fulfil our role. There is also a full induction programme for new governors.
If you are interested in this position, please apply in writing with an outline of the skills you feel you could bring to the role.
Human Resources.
Legal (education, employment, contract).
Site, building and facilities expertise.

The Governors
Contact the Governors on: [email protected]
Oaklands Junior School and Oaklands Infant School now share a single governing body for Oaklands Schools. They are a passionate, diverse group of people, who are all volunteers, with a common interest in the schools, their staff, pupils, buildings and the community for which they form part. Each governor brings different strengths and skills to the Governing Board, but all have a commitment to making Oaklands outstanding.
The full Governing Board meets at least 6 times each year.
The governors focus strongly on three core functions:
Our Governors

SEND
Oaklands Junior School strives to provide the highest standard of learning in an environment where children can flourish and develop, both academically and socially, within a welcoming and caring community. Our aim is to equip each child with the opportunities to develop a sense of self-respect and self- confidence along with a lifelong love of learning. Within a culture of celebration, every child is motivated and supported as they work towards achieving personal excellence.
Examination results show that our children achieve a high standard of academic success which is consistently above the national average. Oaklands Junior School offers a broad, balanced curriculum which is carefully planned to stimulate interest and encourage children of all abilities to reach their full potential in every aspect of school life. Learning should be an exciting experience and to this end the children are provided with many opportunities to have ‘fun’ whilst they are learning.

Sports Premium Funding
PE & Sports Premium Funding 2024 – 2025
1. Background to PE & Sport Premium
The Department for Education, Department for Health and Department for Media, Culture and Sport announced in March 2013 that there would be a grant for all primary-aged children delivered through schools. This grant became available in the school year 2013/14 and continues to be available until further notice.
The aims of the grant are to ensure children have the chance to:
Develop a lifelong love for physical activity
2. Budget allocation for the Academic Year 2024 – 2025
Schools with 17 or more pupils receive £16,000 plus £10 per pupil. Funding received for this academic year £18,450
3. Ofsted advice for spending Sports Premium
It is up to individual schools to determine how best to use this additional funding, however in order to achieve the strategic aims of the grant it is recommended that the money is used to promote physical exercise over and above what is provided in the normal curriculum. Ofsted advise that this money should not be used to provide PE supply teachers (or coaches) to cover planning, preparation and assessment (PPA).

Berkshire Under 11 Boys and Girls Hockey Tournament
Published by School on 19/02/2018
On Tuesday 20th February Oaklands attended an Under 11 Hockey Tournament at Reading Hockey Club. This was a very large tournament with 30 teams from across Berkshire. Despite the bitterly cold wind that swept across the pitches the Oaklands Team remained positive and demonstrated great sportsmanship at all times. We initially played 4 matches in the qualifying rounds. We lost two and drew two. The team then moved into the plate competition, in which we lost one and won one. Well done to Patrick D and Oliver F for scoring and also a special mention to Sophie A for her amazing goal keeping skills! Well done Oaklands, you made all your supporters proud!
Team: Joel D, Aaron S, Patrick D, Jasmine L, Sophie A, Oscar H, Thomas N, Oliver F, Harley W, Emily Ri Mr B Hill

Touch Rugby Tournament Furze Platt School
Published by School on 04/10/2017
We went to a girl only touch rugby tournament. All of us learnt a lot and had loads of fun. Some of us had never played rugby before so it was extremely exciting. We all worked very well together. At the start we weren’t really in the rhythm but the more matches we played the better we got. All the teams were very supportive and made everyone feel welcome. At the end all of the teams sat down together. The organiser spoke to us and then handed out some awards to some people who they thought did well. Over all we all enjoyed the tournament and would definitely do it again. Emily R

Year 4 Mixed 7-a-side Football Tournament
Published by School on 05/10/2017
On a glorious Autumn afternoon Oaklands attended a Year 4 mixed football tournament at Reddam School in Sindlesham. All the children played extremely well and they improved dramatically during the course of the tournament. After some early defeats the team managed to snatch a 1-0 win against Finchampstead in their last match. A special mention must go to our two girls, Robyn and Jessie, who played every match. All the children played enthusiastically and quickly learnt the skills of marking and not all running after the ball. This team should go from strength to strength. Thank you to all the parents that came along and supported the squad. Mr Hill

Year 5 / 6 Football v Beechwood
Published by School on 10/10/2017
In the football match, Oaklands Junior vs Beechwood, Oaklands won 2-0 after a tough game. Oaklands dominated the match but Beechwood played well. Each team had a few shots on target and a few wide. Oaklands controlled the ball well in midfield passing it forward as a team. Beechwood’s goalkeeper made some spectacular saves as well as Oakland’s goalie. But we got through later in the game. In the first half Oliver W scored the opening goal and Beechwood almost scored an equaliser. After the break there were some changes from both teams in their defence. Also in the second half Oliver F scored from a passing move. Oakland’s captain Ollie H nearly scored a third but was denied by Beechwood’s goalkeeper. Beechwood nearly conjured up a goal out of nothing in extra time. Anon
